title: Secret Shopkeepers: The Illegal Cats of New York's Bodegas
summary:
Next time you grab a snack at a New York City bodega, look closely at the shelves. That fluffy tabby snoozing on the Doritos? She's not just cute—she's a secret worker, and technically, an outlaw!

Bodegas are small neighborhood shops that sell everything from sandwiches to soap. Many have cats that live there, catching mice and greeting customers. But here's the twist: New York City health rules say animals can't be in stores that sell food. So thousands of these furry helpers are actually illegal.

Dan Rimada loves these cats so much he started a project called Bodega Cats of New York. He wants everyone to know about them. This fall, he's releasing a book with 120 photos of 60 cats from all over the city. You'll meet Oreo in Park Slope and Prince in SoHo. Each cat has a story—some are treated like kings and queens, while others just get by.

Rimada isn't just taking pictures. He's fighting to change the law! Two new bills would let cats stay in stores as long as they're healthy and vaccinated. 'We want to protect what makes New York City feel like home,' Rimada says. 'And that includes taking care of the cats that are a part of it.'

The book comes out in November. Until then, you can follow hundreds of bodega cats on Instagram. Who knew your corner store had such a cool secret?
why_it_matters: This story shows how everyday places can have secrets, and that people can work to change laws to protect something they love, like cats.

background_read: Many small shops around the world keep cats to catch mice, but in New York City, health rules have banned animals from food stores for decades.
Bodegas are a big part of New York City culture, and the cats that live in them have become secret local celebrities.
Dan Rimada, a photographer who loves these cats, is trying to change the law so they can stay in stores without breaking any rules.
Article_Structure: WHO: Dan Rimada and the bodega cats of New York City.
WHAT: A book featuring 60 bodega cats and an effort to pass two bills that would allow cats in stores if they are healthy and vaccinated.
WHERE: Inside bodegas, small food shops, all across New York City neighborhoods like Park Slope and SoHo.
